title: Ten-year follow up of patients with first-episode schizophrenia spectrum disorder from an early intervention service: Predictors of clinical remission and functional recovery
cohort_overlap_notes: Same 148 EASY entrants (1 July 2001 to 30 June 2002, schizophrenia-spectrum) as chan2020 (early intervention group) and chan2022 (EIS group). Participants are near-certainly also inside the larger EASY July 2001 to August 2003 FEP outcome cohort reported by chang2016 (hk_easy_fep_2001_2003); recorded as overlaps_with in report_cohort_map.csv. Not the same sample as chang2016b, which is a later randomised trial of EASY 2-year completers.
notes: Employment is reported ONLY as mean months of full-time employment and mean months of unemployment over the initial 3 years (Tables 1-3, pp. 67-68), used as predictors of 10-year remission/recovery. Employment status WAS collected at the 10-year interview ('Demographic information including age, gender, education level, employment status were obtained', Methods 2.3, p. 66) but no employment count or rate is reported anywhere. No numerator and no denominator recoverable, so report_quantifiable = no and no outcome row is written. 'Months of unemployment including period of unemployment and rehabilitation' (table footnotes), so time in rehabilitation settings is counted as unemployment.

title: Ten-year employment patterns of patients with first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum disorders: comparison of early intervention and standard care services
cohort_overlap_notes: COHORT CONFIRMED, and the report describes TWO separately recruited samples. The early intervention sample IS hk_easy_2001 (EASY, 1 July 2001 to 30 June 2002, schizophrenia-spectrum, 148 identified, 74.3% interviewed, N = 110), identical to chan2019 (which chan2020 cites as reference 22) and to the EIS group of chan2022. The standard care sample is a separately recruited historical control cohort (first presentation to standard care 1 July 2000 to 30 June 2001) and is recorded as hk_standard_care_2000 under D12.5 / codebook rule 11. extraction_reports carries only the index cohort; report_cohort_map.csv is authoritative and carries both.
notes: EMPLOYMENT IS THE STATED OUTCOME BUT NO COUNT IS RECOVERABLE. The 10-year employment history is expressed as months of employment per year, and the reported quantities are (a) hierarchical-cluster memberships (good employment cluster: early intervention 98/145 (67.6%), standard care 76/145 (52.4%)) and (b) mean total months of full-time employment in year 1. A trajectory-cluster membership is NOT a count of people employed at a timepoint and must not be read as one, so no employment prevalence row is written. CONSTRUCT, if a count is ever obtained: 'Patients who were in full-time or part-time competitive paid employment or full-time education (provided by a government-recognised educational institution) at any time during the assessment period were considered as employed for that period. ... Supported employment, volunteer work, working at a rehabilitation centre and part-time education were not included.' (Method, Ten-year employment history, p. 492). That is paid_or_education and explicitly EXCLUDES supported and sheltered paid work, so it could never serve as paid_any.

title: Longitudinal relapse pattern of patients with first-episode schizophrenia-spectrum disorders and its predictors and outcomes: A 10-year follow-up study
cohort_overlap_notes: Re-analysis of the same 148 matched pairs as chan2020: the EIS group is hk_easy_2001 and the SCS group is hk_standard_care_2000, so two rows in report_cohort_map.csv. The analysed sample (n = 209) POOLS the two cohorts and is split by relapse timing, not by service, so it is not a whole-cohort analysis unit for either cohort. Table 1 confirms the composition: early intervention service 72 + 35 = 107, standard care service 81 + 21 = 102.
notes: Employment is reported ONLY as mean months of employment and mean months of unemployment over 10 years, by relapse group (Table 2, p. 4). No count of people employed at any timepoint. Cross-sectional 10-year outcomes are PANSS/SANS/CDS/SOFAS/RFS scores only; the RFS 'Work' subscale is a 1-7 functioning rating, not an employment count. No numerator or denominator recoverable, so report_quantifiable = no and no outcome row is written.

title: Three-year clinical and functional outcome comparison between first-episode mania with psychotic features and first-episode schizophrenia
cohort_overlap_notes: MANIFEST CORRECTED. The manifest recorded this report against hk_easy_2001, but the sample is a DIFFERENT recruited group: 700 patients enrolled in EASY between July 2001 and August 2003 (of whom 515 had schizophrenia or first-episode mania with psychotic features and 420 completed 3-year follow-up), not the 148 schizophrenia-spectrum entrants of 1 July 2001 to 30 June 2002 studied by chan2019/chan2020/chan2022. Different recruitment window and different diagnostic inclusion, so a separate cohort_id (hk_easy_fep_2001_2003) with an overlaps_with row to hk_easy_2001. The two samples almost certainly share the 2001-2002 schizophrenia-spectrum entrants; neither report states the overlap, so it must not be pooled with any hk_easy_2001 result.
notes: The ONLY report in batch F01 with an employment count. Two subgroup results at 36 months (first-episode schizophrenia 111, first-episode psychotic mania 21). Both are BLOCKED (conflict_status = unresolved): the source contradicts itself about what sustained employment counts (Methods include full-time study, both table footnotes omit it) and, for the schizophrenia subgroup, about its denominator (111 with a printed 30.0% is impossible on the stated n = 374). 36 months falls in NO prespecified horizon band (t24m closes at 30, t60m opens at 48), so this report contributes to no landmark horizon even if the conflicts are resolved.

title: Prediction of functional remission in first-episode psychosis: 12-month follow-up of the randomized-controlled trial on extended early intervention in Hong Kong
cohort_overlap_notes: MANIFEST CORRECTED. The manifest recorded this report against hk_easy_2001. It is not that sample: it is a single-blinded randomised controlled trial (n = 160; extended EI 82, step-down care 78) recruited from patients who had ALREADY COMPLETED the 2-year EASY programme, so entry to this cohort required 2 years of prior EASY treatment. Recruitment dates are not stated in this report (methods are deferred to Chang et al. 2015), and the service is described as five clinical teams against the four teams described for 2001-2002 in chan2019/chan2020, so a shared recruitment era cannot be assumed. Separate cohort_id hk_easy_ext_rct, no overlaps_with row asserted because overlap cannot be established from this report.
notes: Employment appears ONLY as one necessary component of the composite functional remission outcome: FR required SOFAS > 60, RFS subscale thresholds AND being 'engaged in competitive employment (full-time or part-time work or studying)' at BOTH 6 and 12 months. Only the composite is counted (31/156, 19.9%); the employment component is never counted on its own. A composite of employment AND functioning-scale thresholds is not an employment construct and has no value in the outcome_construct vocabulary, so no outcome row is written. Note also that this source calls full-time study 'competitive employment', which the review's vocabulary does not.
